text: You just heard a bang, and your plane is dropping. Here's what you do.
The masks drop. Put yours on first. Up here, you can black out in under thirty seconds.
Pull your seat belt low and tight across your hips.
Now brace. Feet flat on the floor, head down against the seat in front of you.
That stops your body from whipping forward when you hit.
You made it, but the cabin is filling with smoke. Stay low. The clean air is near the floor.
You can't see a thing. That's why smart flyers count the rows to the exit when they sit down.
Leave your bag, jump on the slide, and run. Planes are built so everyone can get out in ninety seconds.
In American airline accidents, about ninety-five out of a hundred people survive.
And that's what to do when your plane is going down.
